look_here_first: Woody catclaw mimosa with many pairs of pinnae, strongly hooked infrastipular prickles, pale pink to whitish flower heads, and pods constricted between seeds.

key_traits.label: Family pattern
key_traits.text: Fabaceae/Mimosa: bipinnate leaves, pulvini that can drive touch-sensitive movement in several species, globose heads of many tiny flowers, and segmented/prickly legumes. Habit, prickle placement, pinna count, and pod structure are especially useful.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: 1–2 strongly recurved prickles near leaf nodes

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: pale pink to whitish globose heads

lookalikes.differences: Compared with M. texana, it usually has more pinnae and leaflet pairs, prickles arising near the stipules, and more strongly constricted pods.
